paragraphs: Polco sells community engagement and analytics software to city and county governments, with a suite of tools organized around the work of local government departments. The platform is presented as a way to connect residents with the governments that serve them.

Residents use it to weigh in and to see how their own town is doing. On the government side the toolset spans community analytics, simulation and resident engagement. Officials can compare local results against national standards. An assistant called Polly reads survey responses, demographic shifts and economic indicators and pulls out community trends. A second agent, Grace, works on grant applications by finding funding opportunities and helping draft them.

The company puts its user base at more than a thousand communities. Cities, counties and other organizations make up that base. Polco says its AI is built only for local governments and public agencies rather than adapted from a general tool. It describes that work as grounded in decades of public administration research. The company also states that it does not sell user data.
